title: Origins of chess (chaturanga)
summary: Chess developed from chaturanga, an Indian army game of infantry, elephants, cavalry and chariots played on an eight-by-eight board. World History Encyclopedia places its origin in northern India during or shortly before the 5th century CE, while a Salar Jung Museum exhibit dates its birth to the 6th-century Gupta period; it then passed to Persia as chatrang. The date and place are uncertain.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia: "somewhere during or shortly before the 5th century CE"; Salar Jung Museum exhibit: the 6th century. The span 400-600 covers both.

as_recorded.value: somewhere during or shortly before the 5th century CE

where.modern_name: India (sources name northern India / India; no site)

importance.justification: The origin of a game that spread worldwide.

reviewer_note: Tradition and scholarly estimate, not a dated event. The pin is the Wikidata point for India with 1500 km uncertainty because sources name only "northern India" or "India"; it marks no site. Dates conflict (5th vs 6th century) and the span covers both.
